title: eval-harness: add per-prompt metrics CI hook + prompt-set quality gating
author: Lina Martinez
description:
Motivation: Several production regressions in model outputs have been traced back to subtle prompt-set changes (tokenization, example ordering, and minor template edits). We need a lightweight CI hook that computes per-prompt metrics (accuracy/score delta, unpredictability, and token-shift) for every candidate model change and a gating layer to fail PRs when prompt-set quality drops beyond configured thresholds. This PR introduces a per-prompt metrics CI hook plus a small quality-gating library and docs.

What this changes: Implements a GitHub Actions/CI hook (ci/workflows/eval-harness.yml) that invokes a new hook script (eval-harness/.github/hooks/per_prompt_metrics.py). The hook runs the eval-harness on a curated set of prompt-sets, emits per-prompt metrics into a compact JSONL artifact, compares against baseline metrics stored in eval-harness/benchmarks/prompt_sets/baseline.jsonl and evaluates configured thresholds in eval-harness/evals/prompt_quality/gating.py. We also add unit tests for the metric computation and gating behavior, and docs explaining how to add new prompt-sets and adjust thresholds.

Checklist: - [x] Core metric computation (score delta, token-shift, per-prompt variance) - [x] CI hook wiring + artifacts - [x] Quality gating logic and configurable thresholds - [x] Unit tests + small synthetic prompt-sets - [x] Docs and runbook for incident followups - [x] Backwards-compatible: default gating is permissive for existing repositories to avoid noisy failures

Backward compatibility and rollout: The gating is behind a repository-level opt-in flag and by default will only annotate PRs with failures as warnings during a 2-week monitoring window. After monitoring, the repo admin can flip enforce=true to make gates block merges. We plan a staged rollout: internal infra repos (1 day), core redwood repo (1 week opt-in), then enforced after monitoring and stakeholder sign-off.

Testing: Added unit tests covering metric edge cases and a small integration test that runs the CI hook against a synthetic prompt-set with an intentional regression. Ran the full GitHub Actions matrix on a fork; initial run showed a lint failure which was fixed in a follow-up commit. Final CI matrix is green.

Related: ENG-1423 (prompt-set regression detection), SUP-4123 (support case referencing a prompt-ordering regression).
